test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The inmates of the house __have slept__ when the thief entered.
solution:
The correct answer is- 'were sleeping.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We know that when one action was taking place in the past at the same time another event takes place simultaneously, we past continuous tense for the continuous action. And these actions are connected by the conjunction '**when' **or '**while**.'

 
 
• Example: 

 
 
• *​I was sleeping **when **he called.*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​*So to make the sentence correct replace the **present perfect tense **with the **past continuous tense**.
 
• Thus *option 2 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *The inmates of the house **were sleeping **when the thief entered*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's understand the use of the conjunctions **when **and **while**.

 
 
• We can use either **when **or **while **if the *subordinating conjunction *(**when **or **while**) comes before the **continuous action**.

 
 
• **Example:** 

 
 
• *She got into an accident **while **she was driving home.*
 
• *She got into an accident **when **she was driving home.*
 
 
 
 
 
• if we change the sentence around, and the *subordinating conjunction *(**when **or **while**) comes before the *single action*, **not **the *continuous action*, we must use **when**.
 
 
• **Example:** 
 
 
• *She was driving home **when **she got into an accident.*
